A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ContextGen work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on LAMICBench++, COCO-MIG, and LayoutSAM-Eval, alongside attention-layer and DPO ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds positional-indexing ablations, a user study, additional comparisons, and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: ContextGen retains its backbone, CLA/ICA masks and layer placement, positional indexing, layout-composition procedure, and DPO approach. V2 clarifies the final DPO configuration without establishing a changed method. MS-FLUX is introduced as a comparator.

E1.justification: IMIG-100K and the three benchmark datasets remain. V2 adds human image-quality assessment with ten reviewers and targeted prompt-flexibility and overlapping-layout scenarios (B.3.2–B.5). Expanded descriptions of dataset styles and face annotations do not establish changed training coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds 3DIS to the COCO-MIG and LayoutSAM-Eval comparisons and introduces the trained MS-FLUX comparator (Table 7). Supplementary LAMICBench++ comparisons are replaced by grids featuring LAMIC, DreamO, UNO, and Kontext (Figures 15–16). Table 1 retains its comparator set.

E3.justification: V2 adds FID evaluation and a user-study protocol covering 40 sets of seven outputs, with ten reviewers selecting two best and two worst images per set. New experiments introduce positional-index controls and MS-FLUX training for 50K steps with rank-512 LoRA. Existing benchmark definitions and ContextGen's stated main training budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds tests of positional offsets and editing tokens, DPO quality assessed through FID and human preferences, final-model DPO comparisons, prompt-driven flexibility, and ICA's preservation of occluded details. B.7 additionally tests transfer of a grounding-resampler strategy to FLUX. The original layer-placement and DPO beta sweeps remain.

E5.justification: V2 newly reports sampling 20 input/seed sets from each of two benchmarks for the user study. V1 already disclosed fixed-seed DPO illustrations. Neither version reports repeated-training-run statistics, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the additional seed information does not establish increased replication of existing experiments.

E6.justification: Retained numerical entries in Tables 1–4 and the detailed COCO-MIG table are unchanged. New results include positional-ablation IDS of 21.54 without x/y offsets versus 32.72 for the full strategy, FID of 55.32 at beta 500, and user preference of 0.54 at beta 100, plus 3DIS and MS-FLUX results. Qualitative outputs are added or replaced. The introduction also corrects the I-SR advantage from 3.4 to 3.3 percentage points.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4, cumulative positional offsets, and the Appendix A.2 layering-priority formula remain unchanged. The added analyses introduce no new theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution summary drop explicit superiority in overall visual quality and emphasize layout control and identity preservation. The principal claims concerning ContextGen, CLA/ICA, IMIG-100K, and state-of-the-art performance remain.

C2.justification: V1 describes ICA as significantly outperforming CLA alone; v2 acknowledges similar aggregate scores and argues its importance lies in rare overlapping cases. V2 also adds interpretations of FID limitations, prompt-dependent flexibility, layer-specific attention effects, and MS-FLUX failure. The original limitations paragraph is retained as Appendix E.

D1.justification: V2 distinguishes rank-256 DPO ablations from rank-512 final-model tuning, supplies MS-FLUX implementation code and parameters, and details dataset prompt diversity, face alignment, spatial annotations, and quality filtering. These are additional disclosures rather than established pipeline changes. Conversely, v1's project link and explicit dataset-release promise are omitted.

R1.justification: New Appendix C.1 substantially expands dataset positioning against OmniGen, UNO, XVerse, and MS-Diffusion, discussing annotation and reference-target variation limitations. B.7 adds an argument for the backbone-specific value of ContextGen's mechanisms. CR-FIQA and facexlib are newly cited; the main related-work section is largely retained.

P1.justification: The main section order and most existing prose remain. Edits include localized abstract, conclusion, and ablation rewrites, terminology corrections, and cross-references. Appendix material is regrouped: DPO moves from A.3 to B.3, benchmark demonstrations move into D, and dataset documentation receives a separate section.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 5–7 and extensive DPO, prompt, overlap, and dataset illustrations. The earlier supplementary LAMICBench++ grid is replaced by Figures 15–16, comparison grids gain 3DIS columns, and existing displays are rearranged. Table 2's benchmark caption is corrected; the detailed COCO-MIG table moves from Table 5 to Table 8.

improvement.justification: The positional ablations, DPO user study, and clearer dataset and training documentation improve validation and transparency. However, overlap evidence remains limited to selected qualitative cases, and new Table 7 leaves aggregation unclear: MS-Diffusion identity scores match Table 1's More Subjects subset, while ContextGen's match Table 3's aggregate results. Removal of the project link also reduces access information. The net improvement is therefore limited.
